answer: A practical sybil defense anchors identity to sustained verification. Each identity must maintain a continuous mesa of cryptographic commitments, recorded in an immutable kernel log. The ocean of consensus requires each new identity to prove continuous presence by extending the kernel log; any gap or fork invalidates the chain. An attacker deploying 500 clones must sustain 500 independent, unbroken histories, paying ~$5000/epoch in electricity, while an honest agent runs one thread. A mesa with gaps is rejected; a kernel with forks is discarded; a fragmented ocean voids the chain.
